messages.text: Red Roses' 41-game unbeaten run ended in dramatic fashion

metadata.summary: England's 41-game unbeaten run is over after they were stunned by a late rally from Canada, the Red Roses falling 24-21 in their WXV Global Series clash in Toronto.
metadata.content: WXV Global Series: England stunned by a late rally from Canada as Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten run ends with 24-21 loss | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content WXV Global Series: England stunned by a late rally from Canada as Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten run ends with 24-21 loss Canada’s women snapped world champion England’s 41-match unbeaten run with a 24-21 victory in Toronto on Friday Saturday 17 October 2026 07:53, UK Image: Canada ended England's 41-game unbeaten run England's 41-game unbeaten run is over after they were stunned by a late rally from Canada, the Red Roses falling 24-21 in their WXV Global Series clash in Toronto. Shoshanah Seumanutafa came off the bench to score the match-winning try in the 77th minute to hand England their first defeat since the 2022 World Cup final. Following a draw in their previous clash last month in Exeter , Canada looked up for the challenge early as they opened the scoring through Savannah Bauder in the 15th minute. messages.text: Gloucester claim thrilling draw against Champions Cup holders Bordeaux

metadata.summary: Will Trenholm’s brace was not enough to help Gloucester pull off a stunning upset against Champions Cup holders Bordeaux, as they were forced to settle for a 36-36 draw after a dramatic contest.
metadata.content: Champions Cup: Gloucester claim thrilling draw against holders Bordeaux | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Champions Cup: Gloucester claim thrilling draw against holders Bordeaux Will Trenholm scores a brace of tries as Gloucester fall just short of beating Champions Cup holders Bordeaux in a thrilling 36-36 draw; Edinburgh suffered a 27-17 defeat against Toulon in their Challenge Cup opener Friday 16 October 2026 22:53, UK Image: Will Trenholm celebrates as Gloucester draws with Bordeaux in the Investec Champions Cup Will Trenholm’s brace was not enough to help Gloucester pull off a stunning upset against Champions Cup holders Bordeaux, as they were forced to settle for a 36-36 draw after a dramatic contest. George Skivington's team pushed the French outfit all the way during a pulsating European tie at Kingsholm Stadium. Gloucester held a 24-17 lead at half-time before Trenholm crashed over twice, but a double by Louis Bielle-Biarrey salvaged a share of the spoils for visiting Bordeaux. messages.text: Dubois and Wardley both career heaviest for heavyweight title rematch

metadata.summary: Both Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley weighed in at a career heaviest for their WBO heavyweight championship rematch.
metadata.content: Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley both career heaviest for heavyweight title rematch | 'Definitely not going the distance' | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley both career heaviest for heavyweight title rematch | 'Definitely not going the distance' Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley hit the scales for their world championship rematch; Dubois and Wardley both came in at their respective career heaviest weights on Friday; Daniel Dubois defeated Fabio Wardley in a thrilling WBO heavyweight title clash in May John Dennen Sports Journalist @johndennen Friday 16 October 2026 20:04, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fabio Wardley and Daniel Dubois weigh-in and face off ahead of their heavyweight title clash tomorrow night. Both Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley weighed in at a career heaviest for their WBO heavyweight championship rematch. London's Dubois had scaled a career heaviest for their first fight and he topped that at 253.9lbs for Saturday's rematch while Wardley was 248.3lbs. Dubois said that means they're both going for power in this fight. "I'm ready to go, ready for my job," he told Sky Sports . "I'll break him down, break him down. Like last time, but better this time." messages.text: Carrick opens door for January transfer activity at Man Utd

metadata.summary: Manchester United will look at trying to strengthen in the January transfer window, according to head coach Michael Carrick, as the club draw up plans to improve the defence over the next year.
metadata.content: Man Utd transfer news: Michael Carrick opens door to January signings ahead of planned defensive rebuild | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Man Utd transfer news: Michael Carrick opens door to January signings ahead of planned defensive rebuild Man Utd plan to improve their defensive options, particularly at left-back and centre-back, over the next two transfer windows after focusing on attack and midfield over the last two seasons; watch Leeds vs Man Utd on Sunday, live on Sky Sports from 1pm; kick-off 2pm Saturday 17 October 2026 10:36, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Carrick gives his thoughts on Lisandro Martinez, following the Argentine's comments about the club's hierarchy after the Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid. Manchester United will look at trying to strengthen in the January transfer window, according to head coach Michael Carrick, as the club draw up plans to improve the defence over the next year. Lisandro Martinez this week publicly called out the club's hierarchy for a lack of investment in the summer window, in which United (£163m) were outspent by promoted sides Hull (£173m) and Ipswich (£211m) despite qualifying for the Champions League. United focused on the midfield rebuild, bringing in Youri Tielemans (£35m), Andrey Santos (£50m) and Carlos Baleba (£70m) for a combined £155m, rather than addressing the lack of depth at left-back and up front. messages.text: Lions forward Andrews dies suddenly ahead of match in France

metadata.summary: Lions player Hyron Andrews has died suddenly in France, where the team were preparing for a Champions Cup fixture.
metadata.content: Hyron Andrews: South African rugby side Lions confirm sudden death of player ahead of Champions Cup match in France against La Rochelle | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Hyron Andrews: South African rugby side Lions confirm sudden death of player ahead of Champions Cup match in France against La Rochelle Hyron Andrews died suddenly in France at the age of 31; the Lions say their Champions Cup game on Saturday against La Rochelle will go ahead in honour of the forward; Andrews previously played for English club Sale Sharks Friday 16 October 2026 15:57, UK Image: Hyron Andrews has died aged 31 Lions player Hyron Andrews has died suddenly in France, where the team were preparing for a Champions Cup fixture. A statement from SA rugby said that Andrews "passed away tragically, following an accident" and that he had "died after falling" at the team hotel. Following French media reports that a Lions player had passed away, the Lions released a separate statement in the afternoon that named Andrews. The 31-year-old South African second-row forward had spent the previous two years of his career playing for Sale Sharks in England before returning home this summer to join the Lions. The Lions said Saturday's match against La Rochelle will go ahead "in honour of Hyron". Twitter This content is provided by Twitter , which may be using cookies and other technologies. messages.text: England record dominant win over Wales at Women's Rugby League World Cup

metadata.summary: Connie Boyd and Anna Davies both notched hat-tricks as England recorded a dominant 70-6 rout of Wales in their opening game of the Women's Rugby League World Cup.
metadata.content: England 70-6 Wales: Connie Boyd and Anna Davies hat-tricks propel Lionesses to dominant opening Women's Rugby League World Cup win | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England 70-6 Wales: Connie Boyd and Anna Davies hat-tricks propel Lionesses to dominant opening Women's Rugby League World Cup win England record a dominant 70-6 win over Wales in their opening match of the Women's Rugby League World Cup; Former Lioness Paige Travis secured Wales' first ever try at the tournament; England take on a vaunted Australia side on October 25, with Wales facing Samoa the day before Noah Langford Sports Journalist Saturday 17 October 2026 09:45, UK Image: England face a vaunted Australia side in their next World Cup match Connie Boyd and Anna Davies both notched hat-tricks as England recorded a dominant 70-6 rout of Wales in their opening game of the Women's Rugby League World Cup. The Lionesses took the lead just four minutes into the game and never let up, scoring 13 tries in a sensational victory against a weak Welsh side that lacked quality in both attack and defence. Boyd, Davies, and Isabel Rowe stood out, with the latter ending the match with a 26-point haul after scoring two tries and recording nine successful conversion attempts. The win gives Stuart Barrow's side a valuable platform in the pool stage ahead of their next match against a vaunted Australia side next Saturday, while Wales have work to do against Samoa to stand any chance of progressing.
